title: Cloudflare Brings On-Demand CPU and Memory Profiling to Production Workers
gist: On October 9, 2026, Cloudflare launched on-demand CPU and heap-allocation profiling for production Workers and Durable Objects. Profiles are captured from already-running isolates and shown as flamegraphs in the Workers Observability dashboard or the cf CLI. Cloudflare's own use found a recursive JSON replacer it says it made 2.7x faster and cut one Worker's p99.9 memory from 133 MB to 118 MB, under the 128 MB limit, though on-demand capture is not yet continuous profiling.

insights.claim: Cloudflare launched on-demand CPU and memory (heap-allocation) profiling for Workers and Durable Objects on October 9, 2026. Developers capture interactive flamegraphs through the Workers Observability dashboard or the cf CLI, and can download the profiles for offline analysis.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Cloudflare is building out its developer platform's observability stack, which makes Workers more viable for production workloads where performance matters.
insights.locator: Cloudflare has introduced on-demand CPU and memory profiling

insights.claim: Cloudflare Workers profiling targets an already-running isolate instead of starting a fresh one, so developers see code running under real production traffic. Durable Objects can also be profiled by specific named instance, which helps with problems in stateful workloads.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Profiling production traffic directly removes the need to reproduce issues locally, which is a differentiator for edge serverless platforms.
insights.quote: The key distinction is that profiling targets an already-running isolate rather than starting a fresh one.
insights.locator: The key distinction is that profiling

insights.claim: Cloudflare Workers profiling has prerequisites: the target must receive enough traffic during the capture window, and TypeScript developers should enable source maps so function names are readable.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Low-traffic Workers get less value from on-demand profiling.
insights.locator: The key distinction is that profiling

themes.theme: Engineering profiling on a distributed edge

insights.claim: Because a Cloudflare Worker script can have many isolates across data centres and machines, a profiling request must identify the requested Worker version and find a suitable active isolate. Durable Objects are stateful and can move between locations, so Cloudflare routes the profiling request to the machine that hosts the specific object.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Edge distribution makes standard tooling such as profilers harder to build, which raises the engineering moat for platforms that solve it.
insights.locator: The implementation must account for Workers

insights.claim: For CPU profiling, the Cloudflare Workers runtime starts a V8 profiler that samples every millisecond, releases the isolate lock while requests keep executing, and reacquires the lock only to stop profiling and collect results, so normal request processing is not suspended during the capture.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Low-overhead capture makes it safe to profile in production without degrading the traffic being served.
insights.locator: The runtime does not hold an isolate lock

insights.claim: CPU and memory profiles answer different questions: CPU profiles sample call stacks to show where execution time goes, while memory profiles attribute allocations to functions. A function can use a lot of CPU while allocating little memory, or the reverse, so choosing the right profile narrows a performance investigation to the actual bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: A diagnostic heuristic: match the profile type to the resource under pressure before optimizing.
insights.locator: CPU and memory profiles also answer

insights.claim: Profiling a Cloudflare R2 binding Worker found a recursive JSON replacer that repeatedly traversed nested data. Cloudflare says fixing it made the function 2.7 times faster.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Profiling can surface large, cheap wins in serverless code where CPU time drives billing and limits.

insights.claim: Cloudflare's CPU profiling exposed an unnecessary duplicate metrics call that accounted for about 1% of a Worker's CPU time.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Instrumentation itself is a measurable source of CPU overhead in production services.

insights.claim: Cloudflare memory profiling found that partially disabled Prometheus instrumentation was still consuming substantial memory. Cloudflare says removing the remaining code cut the Worker's 99.9th-percentile memory from 133 MB to 118 MB, below the 128 MB Worker limit.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: The 128 MB Workers memory cap is a real constraint, and observability libraries can push workloads over it.
insights.quote: reduced the Worker's 99.9th-percentile memory usage from 133 MB to 118 MB, bringing it below the 128 MB limit
insights.locator: Memory profiling identified a separate problem

themes.theme: Positioning against existing tools and limitations

insights.claim: Cloudflare's profiler complements rather than replaces existing tools: Chrome DevTools handles local CPU profiling but struggles to reproduce production traffic and data, and pprof offers powerful offline analysis and can read downloaded Cloudflare profiles. Cloudflare's main differentiator is starting a profile on live Workers and Durable Objects from its existing operational interface.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Supporting the pprof format keeps Cloudflare compatible with the standard profiling toolchain instead of locking users in.

insights.claim: Profiling complements logs, metrics and distributed tracing: those tools show when a service is slow or using too many resources, while a profile pinpoints the functions responsible.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Profiling is emerging as a further layer of the observability stack beyond logs, metrics and traces.
insights.locator: The feature also complements logs, metrics

insights.claim: Cloudflare's on-demand profiling is not continuous monitoring: short capture windows can miss intermittent problems, and heap profiles record allocations during the capture rather than a full picture of retained memory. Cloudflare says it is working toward continuous profiling.
insights.speaker: Craig Risi
insights.so_what: Continuous profiling would push Cloudflare further into territory held by dedicated observability vendors.
insights.quote: On-demand capture is not continuous monitoring.
insights.locator: On-demand capture is not continuous monitoring.
